title: The Anatomy of a Cryptocurrency Pump-and-Dump Scheme

extraction.methodology_summary: We develop a predictive random forest and LASSO-GLM model that utilizes coin features and market movements prior to an anticipated cryptocurrency pump-and-dump event to predict the target coin likelihood. The strategy pre-purchases coins whose predicted pump likelihood exceeds a specific threshold before the coin announcement is broadcasted on Telegram channels. Performance is evaluated out-of-sample using chronologically consecutive training, validation, and test datasets.
extraction.data_period: June 17, 2018 to February 26, 2019, tick-by-tick and hourly
extraction.universe: Cryptocurrency coins listed on the Cryptopia exchange

performance_metrics.context: Test sample period of two and a half months using RF1 model with a threshold value of 0.3
performance_metrics.evidence_quote: The return on the investment amounts to 60% (0.96/1.61) over the test sample period of two and a half months.

key_findings: Machine learning classification models like random forests can successfully predict cryptocurrency pump-and-dump target coins with an area under the ROC curve exceeding 0.94.
Market movements and returns occurring shortly before a pump-and-dump announcement are significantly more important for prediction than longer-term features.
A simple trading strategy based on random forest pump likelihood predictions can generate robust out-of-sample returns.
Pump-and-dump organizers systematically prefer obscure, small-market-cap coins with low liquidity.
limitations: Lack of precise trader ID tracking prevents exact matching of individual buy and sell transactions for actual participant profits.
Large purchase orders prior to a pump in liquid exchanges can move the market and cause pump organizers to cancel or switch coins last-minute.
